item.title: Governing in crises: Rural school board experiences of urbanisation during Covid-19
item.description: Encroaching urbanisation into small and rural communities across Aotearoa New Zealand is becoming increasingly common. This phenomenon is the result of multiple crises: strong and continued population growth, a housing shortage, rising housing unaffordability, and Covid-19. This paper offers a critical analysis of how these intersecting crises have intensified existing inequities during the Covid-19 pandemic. item.title: Integration of Ifugao Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Practices (IKSPs) in teaching Philippine studies in multicultural classrooms
item.description: Elements of culture and indigenous knowledge are integral to instruction and foundational to meaningful learning experiences. Using an embedded mixed-method design, this study examined instructional strategies and their extent of usage in integrating Ifugao indigenous knowledge systems and practice (IKSPs) in the teaching of Philippine Studies at the Ifugao State University-Potia Campus. item.title: Protecting New Zealand's agricultural legacy through education
item.description: Renowned globally as a country that produces high quality goods, New Zealand has a reputation second to none when it comes to science and research related to increasing primary produce. Hence, New Zealand’s reliance on export of primary produce to drive the economy is no secret. However, education related to protecting this industry appears to be scant, including in schools. item.title: The impact of digital technologies on children and adolescents in Aotearoa New Zealand
item.description: The use of digital technologies is increasing in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ) schools to support future-focused learning and allow students to gain 21st century skills that can enable them to participate and thrive in a digital future. item.title: Understanding inspiring teaching and learning in mathematics through prospective teachers’ experience
item.description: Understanding how mathematics teacher educators (MTEs) inspire prospective mathematics teachers (PMTs) is essential for advancing mathematics pedagogy and developing future mathematics. item.title: Development of a questionnaire for understanding mathematics teachers' situated learning practices in the Philippines
item.description: This study sought to understand Philippine mathematics teachers’ practices in relation to situated learning theory (SLT) by developing and administering a questionnaire. item.title: Your words matter: The language of fractions
item.description: This article is based on the main finding of an action research study that investigated how primary school teachers could improve the teaching of fractions. The study primarily focused on what pedagogical strategies might be employed when shifting teaching and learning from procedural application to conceptual understanding. item.title: Intermediate Phase mathematics teachers’ conceptions of learner-centred teaching
item.description: The 2030 Sustainable Development Goals of UNESCO places a focus on quality education for all learners. However, meeting the requirements for quality education seems far-fetched for some developing countries, such as South Africa.
